nodes.title: Sunflower constant

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 4$ there is a real number $c$ with $0 < c < 2$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contains no $k$-sunflower has at most $c^n$ members. Here a $k$-sunflower in a family is a choice of $k$ distinct members whose pairwise intersections are all equal.
nodes.title: The Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower bound for $k \ge 4$

nodes.summary: The proposition asserts that for every natural number $k \ge 4$ there is a real number $c$ with $0 < c < 2$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, every $k$-sunflower-free family of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ has at most $c^n$ members.
nodes.title: Erdős–Szemerédi sunflower conjecture for $k \ge 4$

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. A family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ contains a $k$-sunflower if some subfamily $T \subseteq F$ with exactly $k$ members satisfies $A \cap B = C \cap D$ for all $A, B, C, D \in T$ with $A \ne B$ and $C \ne D$, that is, all pairwise intersections of distinct members of $T$ are equal.
nodes.title: Families containing a sunflower

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers. A family $F$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $k$-sunflower-free if it does not contain a $k$-sunflower.
nodes.title: Sunflower-free families

nodes.summary: Let $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $S$ be a family of subsets of a type $X$. Then $S$ is an $r$-sunflower if $S$ has exactly $r$ members (its cardinality is taken to be $0$ when $S$ is infinite) and any two distinct members $A \ne B$ of $S$ satisfy $A \cap B = \bigcap S$, the intersection of all members of $S$.

nodes.summary: Let $w \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of subsets of a type $X$. Then $\mathcal{F}$ is a $w$-set system if every member $A \in \mathcal{F}$ has at most $w$ elements, where the size of an infinite set is taken to be $0$.
